newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds rise on Fed inaction.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds rise on Fed inaction.

text.p: Argentine bonds were higher in late trading Wednesday as the market applauded the U.S. Federal Reserve's decision to do nothing on interest rates, traders said.
"Basically, the story of the day was the Fed. Although their leaving rates unchanged had mainly been discounted, the fact that nothing did happen still pushed bonds up," one trader said.
Argentina's FRB Brady bond due 2005 rose 1/8 to 94-1/4, while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 added $0.10 to 121.40.
"Locally the main factor is a lack of bad news," a trader said. He added that volume had been fair, with institutional investors buying but not aggressively.
"We may get a bit more turnover tomorrow when the U.S. payroll and employment figures come out," he said.
